from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Data Locality", 
                          ["Space-filling curves preserve crucial spatial locality.", 
                           "Map multi-dimensional data into 1D databases.", 
                           "Hilbert search outperforms inefficient row-major scans."])
        
        # --- Preparation ---
        memory_blocks = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.6, width=0.6, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)])
        memory_blocks.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(memory_blocks))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFAA55")
        grid_map = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)])
        grid_map.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(grid_map, 'D2', 'F4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(grid_map))
        
        # Illustrate mapping (lines from linear to grid)
        arrows = VGroup()
        for i in range(min(len(memory_blocks), len(grid_map))):
            arrows.add(Line(memory_blocks[i].get_bottom(), grid_map[i].get_top(), color="#FFAA55"))
        self.play(Create(arrows))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#55AAFF")
        # Highlight cache locality
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(grid_map[0:3], color="#55AAFF", buff=0.05)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Further Exploration", [
            "Curves enable efficient data compression techniques.",
            "They optimize pathfinding and image processing.",
            "Drones use these paths for scanning fields."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Summarize the paradox of infinite length in finite space
        paradox_text = Text("Paradox: Infinite length, finite space", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_text, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(paradox_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display links to further mathematical exploration
        link_text = Text("Further Exploration: Hilbert, Peano curves", font_size=20, color="#FFFF99")
        self.place_at_grid(link_text, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(link_text))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF99")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out the final visualization
        self.play(
            FadeOut(paradox_text),
            FadeOut(link_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#888888")
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Intuitive Paradox (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive concept: Can a 1D line perfectly cover a 2D area? Start with the prerequisite: The concept of topological dimension vs. Lebesgue covering dimension. Explain that while a line is 1D, it can have an infinite length that 'fills' space.
sections.example: Visualize a single, infinitely long piece of yarn being folded back and forth until it completely covers a square tile.

sections.title: The Recursive Anatomy: Peano & Hilbert (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain the construction process using Iterative Function Systems (IFS). Focus on the 'divide and conquer' strategy: sub-dividing a square into 4 quadrants and connecting them to ensure continuity.
sections.example: Show a Hilbert Curve animation: Start with an 'n' shape. Replace each straight segment with a smaller version of the whole, demonstrating the recursive fractal nature.

sections.title: Mathematical Properties: Continuity vs. Differentiability (2:00-3:15)
sections.content: Highlight the key mathematical tension: These curves are continuous functions, yet they are nowhere differentiable. Explain that they map the interval [0,1] onto the unit square [0,1]x[0,1] in a surjective (onto) manner.
sections.example: Use a 'Pixel Map' visual: An animation showing a single moving dot traversing every single pixel in a 1024x1024 screen without ever lifting its 'pen'.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Data Locality (3:15-4:30)
sections.content: Transition to utility. Explain how these curves preserve 'spatial locality.' By mapping 2D/3D data into 1D, we can store multi-dimensional data in 1D databases while keeping neighbors close to each other.
sections.example: An animation of a Cache Controller (a robot character) trying to find memory addresses. Compare the inefficient 'Row-major' search vs. the efficient 'Hilbert Curve' search.

sections.title: Conclusion and Further Exploration (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize that space-filling curves are not just mathematical curiosities but tools for data compression, image processing, and path optimization.
sections.example: Show a brief montage of a drone using a space-filling path to scan a field efficiently without retracing steps.
